title: Surgical remediation playbook for VPC liveness failures with Terraform-safe rollbacks
creator: Priya Shah
description: Operational runbook + automated remediation design to detect, validate, and safely repair common Private (VPC) liveness failures without broad disruptive changes. Focus is on a minimal blast-radius remediation path that prefers process-level fixes (restarts, config tweaks, route repairs) before Terraform-driven infra changes; where Terraform is required, use guarded applies with drift-safe targets and staged rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Health incidents due to common VPC probe failures can be remediated to green within the SLO window using the playbook steps in >= 90% of simulated failures
Automated remediator run in non-prod applies safe-target Terraform changes and has a tested rollback path in the infra repo CI
All remediation actions produce atomic audit events in CloudTrail/GCP audit logs and attach to the incident ticket with links
No remediation path requires manual SSH to private nodes except in escalated P0 cases
Playbook is reviewed by Security and Network teams and marked approved in Confluence
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: run `redwood infra status vpc <customer-id> --probe-latest` to retrieve probe timestamps and recent failure class
2) Scope blast radius: query `promql:sum by(cluster)(increase(vpc_probe_failures_total{probe=~"(health|liveness|kube-probe)"}[5m]))` to identify affected clusters
3) Verify control plane / API reachability: curl the control-plane health endpoint from the management VPC and from an isolated test-host (commands provided)
4) Quick fixes (non-Terraform): restart the failing agent service (`systemctl restart redwood-vpc-agent`), clear agent KV cache, and re-run probes; document command output
5) Network verification: run `traceroute` and `tcping` between management node and affected nodes; check security group/ACL diffs in the console
6) If config drift suspected: run `terraform plan -target=module.vpc_node[\"<node>\"]` in a disposable workspace and inspect diffs; DO NOT apply without guard approvals

7) Guarded apply: if a Terraform action is required for node recreation, use `terraform apply -target=module.vpc_node[\"<node>\"] -lock=false -auto-approve=false` with the `safe-apply` wrapper which runs preflight checks and writes a transient checkpoint state
8) Automated rollback: if post-apply health metrics degrade, the remediator triggers `terraform apply -state-out=rollback.tfstate rollback.plan` created by the CI safety harness
9) Post-remediation validation: run the synthetic probes and confirm metrics (latency, error-rate) are back to baseline for 15 minutes; annotate incident with Grafana panel snapshots
10) Postmortem triggers: if remediation required more than two Terraform node-targets, escalate to a full incident and create a postmortem within 48 hours
automation_design: Design summary: a small controller (remediator) runs in the Private control-plane namespace and listens to health events. It prioritizes remediation procedures in this order: process restart -> routing/iptables fix -> zone-specific node drain/recreate via Terraform targeted apply -> escalate

Safe-Terraform pattern: use `tf-guard` prechecks (resource age, dependency graph, and concurrency token). The remediator writes a checkpoint file to S3/GS before any `apply` so CI can reconstruct a rollback plan
Canary mode: automated remediator runs in canary for 7 days in non-prod; in prod it only suggests actions and creates a runbook card until sign-off
Circuit-breaker: if more than 3 concurrent Terraform targets are requested, remediator refuses and opens an incident with network and infra on-call
Observability hooks: every remediation step emits structured events to the console audit-log endpoint; incidents include trace IDs for cross-system correlation
implementation_notes: Patch required in infra repo: add `safe-apply` wrapper and `rollback.plan` generator (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/9876)
New Terraform module pattern: `module.vpc_node` needs lifecycle `create_before_destroy = true` and explicit `prevent_destroy` toggles for customer-critical nodes
Add e2e test in infra-acceptance: failure injection harness that simulates `vpc_probe` timeouts and verifies remediator sequence
Permissions: remediator service account must have `iam.serviceAccountActAs` and limited `terraform apply` rights scoped to `module.vpc_node` resources only
Docs: add step-by-step runbook in Confluence page: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PRIV/Runbook+-+VPC+Liveness+Remediation
testing_plan: Stage tests: run in staging with synthetic probe failures for 1000 iterations across three failure classes (agent crash, kv cache corruption, route blackhole)
Load tests: ensure remediator can safely orchestrate up to 50 node repairs per hour in a worst-case degradation scenario without exceeding API rate limits
Chaos test: scheduled chaos run to intentionally break probe responses on a random node and assert the remediator follows non-destructive repair first
Security test: run IAM boundary check and audit-event replay to ensure no action is taken without audit trail
